summary: Teams design and prototype a digital wellness experience for Gen Z called BalanceMe, including an educational website, a mobile app with five screens, and a social media campaign artboard. The project must be submitted as a combined PDF and presented live, with scoring based on technical execution and presentation. Teams must follow all guidelines, including copyright and AI usage policies.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
submission_requirements: Submit one combined PDF file containing Clickable URL to Project Files, Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form
Projects must be viewable on Windows and Mac platforms
Set the access level of your project to one of BPA’s recommended settings
Materials must follow the organization’s BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
what_to_bring: One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for their presentation
competencies: Develop and implement integrated design strategies that maintain consistent branding and visual style across digital, print, and interactive media platforms, employing advanced design principles & elements and layout techniques—including grid systems, hierarchy, and whitespace—for readability and accessibility

Apply audience analysis and user-centered design principles & elements while incorporating accessibility standards (WCAG) and responsive design techniques to create content that is relevant, engaging, and usable for all audiences across devices
Collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary teams and communicate ideas persuasively using digital tools and visual storytelling techniques, adapting style and content to audience and context
Conduct usability testing and gather user feedback to iteratively refine designs, ensuring optimal user experience and accessibility

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy.

Team submitted one (1) combined PDF file containing their Clickable URL to Project Files, Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form.

rubric.description: Strong insight into the audience. Content is engaging, relevant, and consistently tailored across platforms.
Flawless execution — visuals, navigation, and interactions are intuitive, responsive, and polished.
Highly creative and original. Ideas are fresh, engaging, and imaginative.
Exceptional use of design principles. Layouts are cohesive, visually engaging, and enhance user experience across all materials.
Cutting-edge visual trends are seamlessly integrated, enhancing the design’s appeal to modern audiences and building credibility within gaming culture.
Flawless, platform-specific UX that flows cohesively across web, app, and social. User goals are anticipated and met at every touchpoint.
Strong, strategic use of advanced tools or platforms (e.g., Figma prototyping, animation, responsive elements) that elevate the user experience.
UX is seamless, intuitive, and fully aligns with branding and user expectations. Experiences feel complete, logical, and immersive.
The text is clean, polished, and free of grammar, spelling, and punctuation errors.

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Team maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation content flows adequately, and each team member's role is clear and integrated into the presentation. Transitions between speakers and/or points are smooth.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.
At least two original team members were present during the presentation.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes, and the presentation lasted no more than ten (10) minutes.

judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the team within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, contestants may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
No materials may be left with the judges
Only the team captain should complete the submission
Finals may be part of the competition
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
PRESENTATION WILL BE STOPPED AT TEN (10) MINUTES
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged team event
A team will consist of 2 -4 contestants
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy will be disqualified
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
